column1: tags: build, construction, walls, tower, aboveground
description: A constructed surface platform built from the construction family of #build tokens
column2: none of which appear in the other examples. Cw is a constructed wall and rings the perimeter to form the tower shell. Cf is a constructed floor and fills the interior
column3: giving dwarves solid ground to stand on above open space. Cx is a constructed up/down stair placed in the center for vertical access; it connects to the floor above and the floor below at once
column4: which is why a single-level blueprint uses Cx rather than Cu (up stair only
column5: cap the top of a stairwell with it) or Cd (down stair only
column6: cap the bottom). Cr is a constructed ramp and sits in the south wall so dwarves can walk up from ground level onto the platform. The rest of the family
column7: named here so the coverage is complete
column9: used to drop constructions with a linked lever) and D (a trade depot); constructed tracks reuse the same trackNSEW tokens as carved track
column10: not a C token. Placement rules the blueprint cannot enforce: every construction consumes a building material (blocks give the best value
column14: constructions cannot be placed on an existing natural or constructed wall
column15: and floors and stairs are built over open space or channeled tiles. Stage a stockpile of blocks next to the site before you run this
column16: because a tower this size needs roughly forty of them.
